placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an observatory instrument calibration report — a spectrograph tuned to a frequency and verified against reference plates. No existing strata category exists in this repo yet, and none of the standard organizational categories (Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates) exactly or plausibly cover instrument calibration work; it is genuinely its own organizational concern that future calibration envelopes will keep feeding.
placements.title: instrument calibration is its own organizational category, not a subset of proof or product work
placements.frame: does this content concern bringing an instrument or system into verified alignment with a reference standard?

placements.title: calibration only counts once verified against an independent reference and shown to hold across the operating range
placements.frame: was this calibration checked against a trusted reference standard, and does it hold across the full range of conditions the instrument is meant to serve?
placements.why: src-1 asserts the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration and that it was verified against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band — a recurring subject (verification-against-reference as the source of calibration confidence) rather than a one-time fact; the specific 88.4 MHz value and the named reference plates are the evidence for this theme, not leaves of their own. src-2 and src-3 restate the same content in structured labelled-field form (instrument identity, calibration value + verification basis) without adding new thematic content, so they support the same leaf. No existing narrative leaf was available to reuse since the graph is empty for this repo; the strata mint above (Calibration) is the natural home given the content's organizational category.
